claims.text: The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating is relatively homogenized and has limited grain-boundary Cu segregation.
A controlled post-deposition heat treatment can promote Cu migration to grain boundaries in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The heat-treated coating will have Cu-enriched grain boundaries relative to the baseline coating.
Diffusion-assisted deformation is active during sliding at several hundred degrees Celsius.
Increased Cu segregation stiffens the grain boundaries.
Stiffer, Cu-enriched grain boundaries reduce grain-boundary sliding.
Cu-enriched grain boundaries inhibit dislocation nucleation at grain-boundary sites.
Reduced grain-boundary sliding and dislocation nucleation hinder the initiation of plastic deformation.
Cu segregation slows wear by impeding diffusion-controlled mechanisms.
The heat-treated coating will exhibit lower wear volume than the baseline coating during high-temperature sliding.
The heat-treated coating will exhibit less microscopic plastic deformation than the baseline coating during high-temperature sliding.
The predicted effects should occur where diffusion enables noticeable segregation and grain-boundary behavior governs deformation and wear.
At low temperatures, the effect of Cu segregation on wear and deformation may be negligible.
Unintended secondary phases may form and affect the quantitative improvement.
